caption:
He won the Olympic marathon barefoot. And set a world best doing it. 🦶

Rome, 1960. Abebe Bikila, a soldier in Ethiopia's Imperial Bodyguard, was a last-minute addition to the team. The shoes he tried didn't fit right, so he ran the way he trained: barefoot. The race started at 5:30 pm and finished in the dark, the course lit by soldiers' torches. With 500 m to go he broke away near the Obelisk of Axum and crossed the line at the Arch of Constantine in 2:15:16, a world best. Four years later in Tokyo, in shoes and 40 days after appendix surgery, he won again in 2:12:11.
